The tests expect the file to still exist after task_func returns, so do NOT delete it inside the function. The task's 'deleted after use' is handled by the test teardown (which removes the file), not by your code. Your os.remove caused every FileNotFoundError and the existence assertion failure.

Instead: create task_func_data if needed, open 'task_func_data/Output.txt' in append mode, write a header only when the file is empty/new, append randomly generated temperature and humidity rows, close the file, and return the path string 'task_func_data/Output.txt'. Leave the file on disk. Ensure repeated calls append (header written only once) and the returned path matches exactly.

The crash is `total_goals += goals` where `goals` is a dict (e.g. {'Team A': 2, ...}), not an int. The task says "update it with the given goals and penalties" — the inputs are mappings of team->value, and you must merge them into the CSV's per-team rows, not add them as scalars.

Instead: read existing rows into a dict keyed by team (int-cast goals/penalties). For each team in the `goals` dict, add its value to that team's goals (create the row if absent); same for `penalties`. Write the updated per-team rows back to the CSV (keep the header). Return `Counter` of the *totals* across all rows: `Counter({'goals': sum, 'penalties': sum})`. Handle missing file gracefully. Don't collapse the CSV to a single 'Total' row — preserve team rows.

The tensor product was wrong. Hidden tests expect the flattened result to have one element per (i,j) pair of P's rows and T's leading dims, i.e. length = P.shape[0]*T.shape[1] (e.g. 12, not 36). Don't use tensordot over P's last axis; instead compute the product so each P row contracts with T's first axis, giving shape (P.shape[0], T.shape[1], T.shape[2]) then flatten to (-1,1). Verify length matches P.shape[0]*T.shape[1]. Also the KMeans got only 2 distinct clusters from 3 requested (ConvergenceWarning) because flattened values were duplicated/wrong; fixing the product shape should give enough distinct points. Keep fit_predict, title exactly 'KMeans Clustering Visualization', and return (cluster_result, ax). Test with small arrays to confirm cluster_result length equals flattened length.
